sections.h2: What sellers should know in Manheim Township
sections.html:
Manheim Township is a Lancaster County municipality of 43,977 people, sitting directly north of Lancaster city. A certificate of use and occupancy and a 2 percent transfer tax round out the local rules.

Lancaster County also has a separate borough named Manheim, so check the municipality on your tax bill before relying on any local rule here. The township has no ZIP code of its own, so owners carry a Lititz, Lancaster or Leola mailing address depending on where the house sits. Communities include Neffsville, Dillerville and Landis Valley.

A listing, a sale by owner and a direct cash purchase are all open to a seller, and the paperwork below applies to each.

sections.h2: The school district and who bills your taxes
sections.html:
The Manheim Township School District covers exactly the township, so a home inside the boundary is in the district and a home outside it is not. That makes the address check simple for a buyer. Buyers with children usually ask which elementary school serves a street, and the district office can confirm that from an address. The elementary schools are Brecht, Bucher, Neff, Nitrauer, Reidenbaugh and Schaeffer.

The township itself does not bill or collect property taxes. Lancaster County assesses the property, while the elected tax collector and the school district collect the bills. Real estate tax bills combine the county and township taxes and go out by March 1. If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, send the lender a copy of the bill.

Lancaster County reassessed every parcel at current market value, and the new values apply to the 2027 tax year. The previous assessments were based on 2018 values, and the new notices should land near what a property would sell for today.

The county used valid arm's-length residential sales from 2022 through 2024, adjusted for acreage, square footage, porches, garages and bathrooms. State law requires each taxing body to adjust its millage so it does not collect more revenue only because values moved, but the tax on an individual house can still rise or fall. County and municipal millage for 2027 is set near the end of December 2026, and school millage for the 2027-2028 year is set in June 2027. The reassessment does not change 2026-27 school taxes.

The next opportunity for an annual appeal is 2028. Call the Property Assessment Office at 717-299-8381 to ask what applies to a house that sold or changed after the notices went out. Before you price your house, look up your reassessed value on the county property search site, since buyers will do the same.

sections.h2: Inspection and certificate of use and occupancy
sections.html:
The township does not require an inspection before settlement. A certificate of use and occupancy can still be requested by the parties to the deal, and the zoning ordinance has required one for every structure since 1944.

If you need a copy, contact the Code Compliance Department with the property address, the home type (single-family, townhouse or duplex) and whether any part of the basement is finished. Staff check the records and send a copy if one is on file. If none exists, the owner or an agent applies in person at the township office, pays a $50 residential filing fee and books an inspection with a code official.

sections.h2: What does the realty transfer tax cost in Manheim Township?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax is 2 percent of the value transferred. Pennsylvania receives 1 percent, and the township and school district share the other 1 percent.

The Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, at 50 North Duke Street, takes payment as part of recording the deed. Buyer and seller are both liable for it, and the sale contract decides how it is split. Certain family transfers and property passed by inheritance are exempt from the state portion, so ask the recorder before assuming a deed is taxable.

sections.h2: Selling a rental in Manheim Township
sections.html:
Rental properties have needed a township license since 2022, and an annual license costs $50 per building. Each rental unit is inspected at least once every five years, and one- and two-unit buildings have every unit inspected.

  • Owners living more than 25 miles from the township must name a responsible local agent.
  • Inspection fees run from $40 for one unit to $250 for buildings with 51 or more units.
  • The code compliance office handles applications, renewals and de-registration.

A landlord who sells should ask the code office how to de-register or transfer the license, and should hand the buyer the latest inspection results.

Start with the paperwork you can control. Ask Code Compliance for a copy of your certificate of use and occupancy, and if none is on file, book the $50 filing and inspection so a missing certificate does not delay closing. Check whether any lender or buyer wants a copy even though the township does not require one for settlement.

Then gather your tax bills, your payoff statement and, if the house is rented, the license and the latest inspection report. Once you have an accepted offer, the title company prorates taxes and the deed is recorded with the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds, where the transfer tax is paid. Confirm in writing who pays which share of that 2 percent. If you inherited the house, ask the recorder how the exemption works before the deed is drawn.

sections.h2: Which route suits a Manheim Township seller?
sections.html:
The right route depends on the house's condition and your moving date. Putting it on the market reaches more buyers but brings showings and inspection haggling, while a direct cash sale can be timed around your move.

  • Request your certificate of use and occupancy early so a missing certificate does not delay the closing.
  • Look up your 2027 reassessed value on the county property search site and compare it with the price you are weighing.
  • Subtract the 2 percent transfer tax share you agree to, plus any mortgage payoff, to estimate net proceeds.

If a buyer asks for repairs, compare the cost against a quote for selling as-is. Cash Home Buyers CA can provide that quote.

faqs.q: Is Manheim Township the same as the borough of Manheim?
faqs.a: No. Manheim Township is a separate municipality that borders Lancaster city and has its own school district and township government. Lancaster County also has a borough named Manheim.

faqs.q: Does Manheim Township require a certificate of use and occupancy when I sell?
faqs.a: Not as a condition of settlement. The township does not inspect before closing, but buyers or lenders may ask for a copy. If none is on file, the residential filing fee is $50 and an inspection is scheduled.

faqs.q: What do buyers and sellers owe in transfer tax in Manheim Township?
faqs.a: The combined rate is 2 percent of the value transferred. The state gets 1 percent, and the township and school district share the other 1 percent. The Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds collects it.

faqs.q: When did the Lancaster County reassessment take effect?
faqs.a: The new values apply to the 2027 tax year. The next annual appeal opportunity is 2028.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Manheim Township?
faqs.a: The elected tax collector and the school district collect the bills. Lancaster County sets the assessment, and the township does not bill or collect property taxes itself.
